blocks.why: Normal night before a civilised 12:00 local report — no need to cut it short.
Home about 22:40 local off a 11h43 day and out the door again at 06:50 — this is only 6h30 and it's the thinnest night of the month, so bed the moment you're through the door.
Full nine hours to pay back last night's shortfall; the LIS turn doesn't report until 15:25 local.
Sleep the normal night, then use the day off to start dragging bedtime earlier.
Lights out at 20:00 local on your day off — the only way to get a real sleep in front of an 05:40 report, and you'll have been up 12h30 so you will drop off.
Straight to bed after the four-sector FRA day; getting up at 06:00 local keeps the pressure building for tomorrow's very early night.
A proper siesta on the day off to bank an hour ahead of the 16h52 monster on the 7th.
Bed at 20:15 local — you need every minute of this before a 05:40 report that doesn't finish until 22:32.
Home at 23:30 local after nearly seventeen hours on duty; sleep as long as the body will take it.
Another 19:30 local bedtime on the day off to cover the 05:05 LIS report.
Awake since 03:05 local and finished by 10:19 — take a solid mid-morning sleep, it also lets you push tonight later.
Deliberately going to bed late and getting up at 10:00 local, because tomorrow you're airborne until 02:31 and blocking in at 03:01.
In the door at 03:55 local and asleep immediately, but keeping it to under six hours so you can get back down again this evening.
Second sleep of the day off — the only way to flip from a 03:01 finish to an 05:40 report in one calendar day.
Straight home from the FCO turn and 90 minutes down to clear the debt from the split night.
Back on a normal night to reset the body clock before the standby block.
An hour before the 14:00 standby opens, in case they call you out for something that finishes late.
Standby released at 20:00 local, so a straightforward full night.
Early to bed on the day off — you're contactable from 06:00 local and I'm assuming you may have to move to the airport.
This is the single most important sleep of the month: standby releases at 13:00 local and you report at 23:00 for an all-night ARN, so black out the room and treat this afternoon as your night.
Home by 10:00 local having flown straight through the window of circadian low — sleep now while the pressure is still there, and don't fight it awake.
Get one clean night in to pull the clock back to Madrid time after the night flight.
Day-off early night ahead of the 05:05 four-sector day.
Ten hours and a lie-in to 09:00 local — tomorrow you don't get to bed until nearly 06:00.
Nap before you leave for a 15:25 report that ends with a DUB night sector landing at 05:11 — go in with a full tank.
Home at 06:35 local off an all-nighter; sleep through the morning but get up early afternoon so tonight still works.
Full night on the day off to finish the recovery — the BCN turn isn't until midday.
Short BCN day means an early bed is achievable, and you need it for an 06:10 report into a 15h01 DUB double.
Home at 22:05 local after fifteen hours — bed straight away, no unwinding.
Day-off early night for the 05:05 FCO/FRA report.
Getting up at 06:30 local on the day off is deliberate — you need twelve hours of wakefulness to fall asleep at 18:30 tonight.
Bed at 18:30 local for the 04:35 report, the earliest of the month; alarm goes at 02:35 local so nothing later will do.
Forty-five minutes on getting home after fifteen hours awake, just enough to be safe and civil for the evening.
Long night to clear the debt — tomorrow is a late finish, not an early start.
An hour before the 14:40 report; the ARN return blocks in at 00:26 local.
In the door about 01:50 local — sleep now, but keep it to under seven hours so the evening sleep still comes.
Second sleep on the day off to get you round from a 00:56 finish to an 05:05 report.
Short nap after the FCO turn — you're up at 03:05 local again tomorrow and the evening bedtime is going to be a squeeze.
Back-to-back 05:05 reports, so bed at 20:00 local even if you're not tired — you've been awake since 03:05.
Last duty done by 10:07 local; sleep off the accumulated early starts before you do anything else.

conflicts.statement: A 16h52 duty, four sectors, starting at 05:40 local — you'll be awake from about 03:40 local until past midnight, roughly 21 hours, with the last sector landing at 22:02. No sleep plan makes that duty feel short.
options: Ask crewing whether the ARN rotation can be split off or the report moved later
Confirm with the operator whether an FDP extension/discretion is being assumed and on what basis
Take the 06/09 siesta plus a 20:15 local bedtime as planned, and pre-brief the FO to swap sectors for the ARN return
Plan controlled rest in the cruise on both ARN legs

conflicts.statement: Home standby 06:00-13:00 local, then report 23:00 local the same day for an all-night MAD-ARN-MAD finishing 09:10 the next morning. Only 10 hours between standby release and report, and the sleep you need in that gap is a daytime sleep after you've already been up since 04:30.
options: Ask for the standby to be dropped or shortened to a late-start window
Ask for the night pairing to be moved to the 16th so the standby day stands alone
If it stays, protect 14:00-19:45 local absolutely: blackout, phone off after the standby release, no errands
Confirm with the operator how standby time counts against the following FDP

conflicts.statement: AU342 lands at 02:31 local and you're off duty at 03:01 — the whole last sector sits inside the 02:00-06:00 body-time trough after a 13h46 day.
options: Ask whether the second LHR rotation can be flown by the following day's crew
Push the wake-up on the 10th to 10:00 local as planned so you're not 20 hours awake at top of descent
Plan in-seat controlled rest on the outbound AU746

conflicts.statement: You block in at 03:01 local on the 11th and report at 05:40 local on the 12th. The calendar shows a day off in between, but the body clock has to move about nine hours in one go — it can't, so the 11th has to be split into two sleeps.
options: Ask crewing to move the 12/09 FCO turn to an afternoon report
Take the split-sleep plan (02:15-08:00Z then 17:30-01:40Z) and accept a shortened first sleep
Flag it to the operator as a disruptive-schedule combination even if each duty is legal in isolation

conflicts.statement: Off duty 21:43 local on the 1st, report 07:45 local on the 2nd. With 55 minutes each way to MAD that's about 8h10 actually at home and realistically 6h30 in bed, in front of a 10h09 duty to ARN.
options: Ask for the 02/09 report to be pushed back, or the 01/09 LHR rotation to be dropped
Keep the 01/09 evening completely clear — bag packed and uniform out before you leave in the morning
Plan controlled rest on the ARN sectors

conflicts.statement: AU837 from DUB lands at 05:11 local after a 14h16 duty — approach and landing right at the bottom of the circadian dip, having been awake since about 12:00 the previous day.
options: Ask whether the DUB night rotation can be uncoupled from the LHR pair earlier in the duty
Take the pre-duty nap on the 19th and treat it as non-negotiable
Plan cruise controlled rest on both DUB legs

conflicts.statement: An 04:35 local report means an alarm at about 02:35 and leaving home at 03:40. You cannot sleep enough before that no matter how early you go to bed, and it opens a 12h06 four-sector day.
options: Ask for the 26/09 report to be moved later, it's the earliest on the roster
Sleep 18:30-02:35 local on the 25th and keep the whole evening dark and quiet
Accept the plan and add the short recovery nap on landing before driving anywhere

conflicts.statement: 05:05 local reports on both the 29th and the 30th, and the 29th only ends at 12:15 local — the second early start is flown on a night that starts at 20:00 with an alarm at 03:05.
options: Ask crewing to move the 30/09 BCN turn later, it's the last duty of the period
Take the short recovery nap on the 29th, then bed at 20:00 local whether or not you feel tired
Avoid caffeine after about 14:00 local on the 29th so the early bedtime works

conflicts.statement: Duty on the 27th ends 00:56 local on the 28th, then a 05:05 report on the 29th. The single day off has to absorb a late finish and set up an early start, which is two opposite demands.
options: Ask for the 29/09 report to move later
Split the 28th into a post-duty sleep to 09:00 local and a second sleep from 19:30
Keep the 28th free of anything social or evening-based

conflicts.statement: The two SBY lines show a MAD-MAD sector and a duty window but do not say whether it is home standby or airport standby. I have planned for home standby with the option of getting to MAD, and I have taken the report time as the start of the window with no reporting offset applied.
options: Confirm the standby type with crewing before the 13th
If it is airport standby, move the pre-standby nap on the 13th earlier and add 55 minutes of commute to the wake-up
If it is home standby, the plan stands as written

conflicts.statement: AU596 appears twice with different routings (MAD-FCO on 12/09, ARN-MAD on 16/09), as do AU445, AU316 and AU690. I have read them exactly as printed, but it is worth a glance before the day.
options: Cross-check the affected flight numbers against the daily plan when it drops
Report the apparent duplication to crewing so the roster can be corrected if it is a typo

conflicts.statement: 15h01 across four sectors with an 06:10 local report, and the same pattern again on 05/09 (14h14), 19/09 (14h16) and 24/09 (14h16) — four duties over fourteen hours in the month, three of them off early reports.
options: Ask crewing whether the pairing density can be eased in the second half of the month
Plan controlled rest on the second half of each of these duties
Raise it as a cumulative fatigue trend in a fatigue report rather than duty by duty
